sources.entry: Scapple - Practical mind-mapping software with free whiteboard-like layout.

summary.name: Scapple
summary.one_liner: Scapple is a freeform note-taking and mind-mapping app that works like a virtual sheet of paper where you place notes anywhere and link them with lines or arrows.
use_cases: grouping ideas into columns or shapes
summary.what_it_does: Scapple lets you create notes by double-clicking anywhere on the page and connect them by dragging one note onto another, with lines or arrows. Connections are optional and every note is equal, so you decide how ideas relate. The canvas is freeform and effectively unlimited in space. You can stack notes in columns, add background shapes to group them, and customise note appearance. The page also lists moving and arranging notes, full screen mode, exporting or printing ideas, and dragging notes into Scrivener.
notable: Freeform canvas where notes can go anywhere with no forced structure
Connections made by dragging one note onto another
Video tutorial demonstrating the Mac version
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page
Page does not specify which features differ between Mac and Windows versions
